senses.definition: To put to death by stoning, the penalty of the Law or an act of mob 'justice'.

senses.label: Stone God's messengers
senses.definition: To pelt or kill with stones the prophets and servants God sends, a mark of Israel's rejection of them.

background.note: The usual Greek term for the Law's penalty of stoning.

study.summary: μακράν is an adverb meaning far or a long way off, used of literal distance and figuratively of distance from God and his kingdom.

senses.label: Far away (distance)
senses.definition: At a distance in space; with χώρα, a far-off country.

senses.label: Far off spiritually
senses.definition: Distance from God or his kingdom, especially of Gentiles once far off but now brought near; also God being 'not far' from anyone.

background.note: Used with the genitive for being a long way from someone: 'the smith is a long way from us'.

study.exegesisTip: EPH 2:13 and 2:17 echo Isaiah's 'peace to the far and the near', applying 'far' to Gentiles reconciled through Christ.

study.summary: μαργαρίτης is a pearl, prized in the ancient world as a costly jewel and used as an image of supreme value.

senses.label: Pearl as costly jewel
senses.definition: Pearls as luxury adornment and trade goods.

senses.label: Image of great worth
senses.definition: Figuratively, something of supreme value: the kingdom, holy things not to be cast before swine, and the gates of the new Jerusalem.

background.note: Described by ancient naturalists as a precious stone.

study.summary: μέλω, used impersonally as μέλει, means 'it is a concern to someone', i.e. someone cares about something.

senses.label: It matters, one cares
senses.definition: With dative of the person: something is a concern to them, often in a question or denial about whether someone cares.

senses.label: Not swayed by anyone
senses.definition: Idiom 'you care about no one': you are impartial and not influenced by people's status.

background.note: The impersonal construction with dative and περί appears in a first-century letter: 'you care much about me'.

study.exegesisTip: The disciples' accusing 'Do you not care?' (MAR 4:38) contrasts with Peter's assurance that God does care for his people (1PE 5:7).

study.summary: μεταξύ means between (in place or relationship), and as a time word 'meanwhile' or 'next'.

senses.label: Between (place)
senses.definition: In the space separating two things or persons.

senses.label: Between (persons)
senses.definition: Of a relation or dealing between parties, privately or mutually.

senses.label: Meanwhile; next
senses.definition: Of time: in the meantime, or (in later Greek) the following, next.

study.translationNote: In ACT 13:42 'the next Sabbath' is the usual rendering, though some older interpreters took it as 'the Sabbath in between'; verse 44 shows the following Sabbath is meant.

background.note: Common prepositionally with the genitive, e.g. of an agreement made between two parties.

study.summary: μνᾶ is a mina, a unit of money worth 100 drachmas, the sum entrusted to each servant in Jesus' parable of the minas.

senses.label: Mina (sum of money)
senses.definition: A monetary unit of 100 drachmas, roughly a hundred days' wages for a laborer.

study.translationNote: Older versions say 'pound'; modern ones use 'mina' or paraphrase with a sum of money.

background.note: Used as a money unit in loan contracts, with interest reckoned at a drachma per mina per month.

study.exegesisTip: Each servant receives the same modest sum, so the parable stresses faithfulness with what is entrusted until the master returns.
study.caution: Do not confuse this parable with the parable of the talents in Matthew; a talent was a far larger sum.

study.summary: μονογενής means 'only' or 'unique, one of a kind', used of only children and, in John, of Jesus as God's unique Son.

senses.label: Only child
senses.definition: A parent's only son or daughter, heightening the pathos of loss.

senses.label: Unique son of promise
senses.definition: Isaac as Abraham's unique son, the one heir of the promise.
senses.note: Abraham had other sons, so 'unique' rather than 'only' fits best here.

senses.label: Christ, God's unique Son
senses.definition: Jesus as the one and only Son who uniquely shares the Father's nature and reveals him.

study.translationNote: The KJV's 'only begotten' links the word to begetting; most modern versions render 'only', 'one and only' or 'unique', since the word stresses uniqueness of kind.

background.note: Used in early Greek simply of an only child.

study.caution: Scholars debate whether the word implies 'begotten' or only 'unique'. Also, in JOH 1:18 manuscripts differ between 'the only Son' and 'the only God'.

study.summary: μυριάς is a myriad, literally ten thousand, and often an indefinitely vast number.

senses.label: Ten thousand
senses.definition: A precise numeral, as in the value of the burned magic books.

senses.label: Countless multitude
senses.definition: A huge, uncountable number, of crowds, believers, angels or armies; 'myriads of myriads' is beyond reckoning.

background.note: Used as the plain numeral 10,000 in business documents.

study.summary: νῆσος means an island, such as Cyprus, Malta or Patmos, and in Revelation the islands shaken in cosmic judgment.

senses.label: Island (geographical)
senses.definition: A particular island visited or inhabited in the narrative.

senses.label: Islands in cosmic upheaval
senses.definition: Islands moved or vanishing as creation is shaken at God's judgment.

study.summary: νομικός means 'relating to the law' and, as a noun, a lawyer, i.e. an expert in the Mosaic Law.

senses.label: Expert in the Law
senses.definition: A scholar of the Mosaic Law, much like a scribe, often testing or opposing Jesus.

senses.label: Zenas the lawyer
senses.definition: Title of Zenas, a co-worker of Paul, as a legal expert.

senses.label: About the law
senses.definition: Adjective: quarrels concerning the Law, to be avoided as useless.

authorNotes.author: Luke–Acts
authorNotes.note: Luke prefers this term where the other Gospels usually say 'scribe', perhaps clearer to Gentile readers.

background.note: Used of experts in Roman law who certified legal documents.

study.caution: Whether Zenas was trained in Jewish or Roman law cannot be determined.

study.summary: οἰκέω means to live or dwell, used by Paul of spouses living together and, above all, of sin or God's Spirit dwelling within a person.

senses.label: Live, reside
senses.definition: To live with someone (in marriage), or to inhabit a place.
senses.note: In 1TI 6:16 God 'dwells in unapproachable light'.

senses.label: Indwelling sin
senses.definition: Sin as a power that takes up residence in a person and drives their actions.

senses.label: Indwelling Spirit
senses.definition: God's Spirit living in believers, marking them as God's people and temple.

study.exegesisTip: Paul uses the same verb for indwelling sin (ROM 7:20) and the indwelling Spirit (ROM 8:9): the question is which power resides in and governs a person.

study.summary: οἰκονομία means stewardship, the management of a household, and by extension a commission entrusted by God or God's own ordering and plan.

senses.label: Stewardship of a household
senses.definition: The office and duties of a steward managing an owner's property.

senses.label: Commission entrusted by God
senses.definition: The responsibility God has given Paul to administer, especially the proclamation of grace to the Gentiles.

senses.label: God's plan, administration
senses.definition: God's ordering and carrying out of his saving purpose, or the arrangement that works through faith.

study.translationNote: The KJV's 'dispensation' (e.g. EPH 1:10, EPH 3:2) reflects older English for 'administration' or 'stewardship'; modern versions say 'plan', 'administration' or 'stewardship'. In 1TI 1:4 the KJV's 'godly edifying' follows a manuscript reading with a different word.

background.note: Used of the official post of a steward or administrator.

study.caution: The word refers to stewardship and administration, not to a fixed 'age' or period of time, even where it concerns the fullness of times (EPH 1:10).

study.summary: πάντως is an adverb meaning 'certainly, by all means', and with a negative 'not at all' or 'not altogether'.

senses.label: Surely, certainly
senses.definition: Strong affirmation: no doubt, of course.

senses.label: By all means, at any rate
senses.definition: Expressing determination or resolve to achieve something whatever it takes.

senses.label: Not at all; not altogether
senses.definition: With a negative, a complete or partial denial.

background.note: Used in letters for an emphatic 'be sure to', e.g. 'be sure to send me the loaves'.

study.caution: In ROM 3:9 'not at all' is the usual reading, though some take it as 'not altogether'; the sense of the preceding verb is also debated.

study.summary: παρρησιάζομαι means to speak openly and boldly, in the NT almost always of fearless proclamation of the gospel.

senses.label: Proclaim boldly
senses.definition: To preach Christ with courage and freedom despite opposition or danger.

senses.label: Speak frankly
senses.definition: To speak freely and candidly before a person of rank.

background.note: In classical prose it means to speak freely and frankly.

study.exegesisTip: Such boldness is not natural daring: Paul asks for prayer to speak boldly (EPH 6:20) and speaks 'in our God' after suffering (1TH 2:2).

study.summary: πιπράσκω means to sell, including selling a person into slavery and, figuratively, being sold under sin's power.

senses.label: Sell goods, property
senses.definition: To sell possessions for a price.

senses.label: Sell into slavery
senses.definition: To sell a person as a slave; figuratively, to be in bondage to sin.

background.note: The ordinary commercial term for selling goods.

study.exegesisTip: In ROM 7:14 'sold under sin' pictures a slave sold to a master, so that the person is no longer free to do the good he wills.

study.summary: πλατεῖα is a wide street or public square of a town, the open public space where people gathered.

senses.label: Street, public square
senses.definition: A broad street of a town or city, a place of public life and display.

senses.label: Street of the visionary city
senses.definition: The main street of the great city where the witnesses lie, and the golden street of the new Jerusalem.

study.summary: πλεονάζω means to increase, abound or be more than enough, and (once) to make something increase.

senses.label: Increase, abound
senses.definition: To grow greater or be plentiful, of sin, grace, love, fruit and virtues.

senses.label: Have too much
senses.definition: Of a person, to have more than needed.

senses.label: Make to increase
senses.definition: Transitive: to cause someone to abound.

background.note: Used of an amount in excess of what was decreed.

study.exegesisTip: In ROM 5:20 sin 'increased' but grace 'super-abounded' (a stronger word), which ROM 6:1 then guards against abusing.

study.summary: ποικίλος means varied or of many kinds (originally many-colored), used of diverse diseases, desires, trials and teachings, and of God's manifold grace.

senses.label: Various, of many kinds
senses.definition: Diverse sorts of afflictions, sinful desires, trials or strange teachings.

senses.label: Manifold divine gifts
senses.definition: The rich variety of God's miracles and grace.

background.note: Used literally of streaked or spotted goats in an account.

study.exegesisTip: Peter speaks of 'various trials' (1PE 1:6) and God's 'varied grace' (1PE 4:10) with the same word: grace is as many-sided as the trials.

study.summary: προπέμπω means to send someone on their way, escorting them and often supplying what they need for the journey.

senses.label: Escort on departure
senses.definition: To accompany travelers part of the way as they leave.

senses.label: Send on with support
senses.definition: To help on a journey with provisions, money or companions, a standard act of Christian hospitality to missionaries.

background.note: Used in a letter of recommendation for sending people on 'with all honour'.

study.exegesisTip: TIT 3:13 ('so that they lack nothing') and 3JO 1:6 ('in a manner worthy of God') show the word includes practical support for travelling workers.

study.summary: προσφορά is an offering, especially a sacrifice presented to God, and in Hebrews Christ's once-for-all offering of himself.

senses.label: Sacrificial offering
senses.definition: Offerings presented in temple worship under the Law.

senses.label: Christ's self-offering
senses.definition: Christ giving himself to God as the sacrifice for sin, once for all.

senses.label: Gentiles as offering
senses.definition: Paul's ministry presenting the believing Gentiles to God as an acceptable offering.

authorNotes.author: Hebrews
authorNotes.note: Hebrews contrasts the repeated offerings of the Law with Christ's single offering, after which no further offering for sin is needed.

background.note: Used of the bread of presentation in the temple.

study.caution: In ROM 15:16 most take 'offering of the Gentiles' as the Gentiles themselves being offered, not an offering made by them.

study.summary: πρωτότοκος means firstborn, literally the first child, and of Christ his supreme rank and priority over creation and the resurrected.

senses.label: Firstborn child
senses.definition: The first child born to a mother, or the firstborn of Egypt struck at the Passover.

senses.label: Christ's preeminence
senses.definition: Christ as the one with the rights and supremacy of the firstborn: over all creation, first to rise from the dead, and first among many brothers.

senses.label: God's privileged people
senses.definition: Believers as the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in heaven, sharing the heir's privileges.

background.note: The regular Greek rendering of the Hebrew word for firstborn, with its rights of inheritance.

study.caution: In COL 1:15 'firstborn of all creation' does not make Christ the first created being: the next verse says all things were created in him; the term denotes rank and supremacy.

study.summary: σελήνη is the moon, part of God's created order and, darkened or turned to blood, a sign of the coming day of judgment.

senses.label: Moon in creation
senses.definition: The moon as a heavenly body with its own glory, or as an image in visions.

senses.label: Moon in end-time signs
senses.definition: The moon failing to shine or becoming like blood as a portent of the Lord's coming.

background.note: Used in calendars and horoscopes for reckoning days by the moon.

study.exegesisTip: In the new Jerusalem the city needs no sun or moon, because God's glory is its light (REV 21:23).

study.summary: σιγάω means to be or fall silent, whether a crowd hushing to listen, people falling silent in wonder, or a speaker holding his peace in the assembly.

senses.label: Fall silent, keep quiet
senses.definition: To stop speaking or keep silence, often in response to an event, a gesture or a speaker; at LUK 9:36 the disciples keep silent about what they saw.

senses.label: Hold one's peace in worship
senses.definition: Paul's instruction that a speaker refrain from speaking in the gathered church so that worship stays orderly and edifying.

background.note: Used in a court record where an advocate asks why someone had kept silent about a matter.

study.exegesisTip: In 1 Corinthians 14 the same command (σιγάτω, 'let him be silent') is given to tongue-speakers without an interpreter and to a prophet when another receives a revelation, so the word is part of a wider concern for order in the assembly.
study.caution: The command for women to be silent in 1CO 14:34 is much debated: interpreters differ on whether it addresses disruptive questioning, the weighing of prophecies, or all speaking in the assembly.

study.summary: στάσις, literally a 'standing', in the NT usually means a violent uprising or a heated dispute, and once the continued 'standing' of the first tabernacle.

senses.label: Insurrection, riot
senses.definition: A violent public uprising or disturbance against authority, such as the revolt in which Barabbas took part or the riot feared at Ephesus.

senses.label: Dissension, sharp dispute
senses.definition: A fierce quarrel or party conflict within a group, as over circumcision at Antioch or between Pharisees and Sadducees in the Sanhedrin.

senses.label: Standing, continued existence
senses.definition: The state of standing or having a valid place; the first tent still 'has standing' while the old order lasts.

study.exegesisTip: At ACT 24:5 the charge that Paul 'stirs up στάσις' is a political accusation of sedition, the kind of offence Rome punished severely.

study.summary: τάσσω means to put in place, appoint or assign, and also to set or fix something such as a place or a day.

senses.label: Appoint, assign a place
senses.definition: To station or appoint persons to a position or task, whether under authority, as rulers instituted by God, or to a course set by God.

senses.label: Devote oneself
senses.definition: With a reflexive pronoun, to set oneself to a task; the household of Stephanas devoted themselves to serving the saints.

senses.label: Fix, order, arrange
senses.definition: To designate or determine something: a meeting place, a day, a decision or an official order.

background.note: Common of officials 'appointed' to an administrative post.

study.caution: At ACT 13:48 ('as many as were appointed to eternal life') most take the participle as passive, of God's appointing; a minority reads it as middle, 'as many as had set themselves', and the verse figures in debates about predestination.

study.summary: τεῖχος is a wall, especially the defensive wall around a city.

senses.label: City wall
senses.definition: The fortification wall of an earthly city, such as Damascus, through which Paul was lowered, or Jericho, whose walls fell.

senses.label: Wall of New Jerusalem
senses.definition: The great, high wall of the heavenly city in John's vision, with twelve foundations, measured and built of jasper.

background.note: From Homer on the standard word for a city wall.

study.exegesisTip: In Revelation 21 the wall's numbers are built on twelve (twelve foundations, 144 cubits), linking the city to the twelve tribes and twelve apostles.

study.summary: τεκνίον, a diminutive of τέκνον, means 'little child' and in the NT is always a tender form of address to disciples or converts.

senses.label: Little children (address)
senses.definition: An affectionate vocative used by Jesus to his disciples and by apostles to believers in their care, expressing warm, fatherly or motherly concern.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: The favourite address of 1 John, used to introduce warnings and encouragements; it echoes Jesus' own address to the disciples on the night before his death.

background.note: Used in a private letter sending greetings to the writer's children.

study.caution: At GAL 4:19 manuscripts are divided between τεκνία and τέκνα ('children').

study.summary: φθόνος is envy: resentful ill-will at another's good, listed among vices and named as the motive behind handing Jesus over.

senses.label: Envy as a vice
senses.definition: Grudging resentment of what others have or are, listed in catalogues of sins that believers must put away.

senses.label: Out of envy (motive)
senses.definition: In the phrase διὰ φθόνον, envy as the driving motive of an action, as of the chief priests or of rival preachers.

senses.label: Jealous longing (disputed)
senses.definition: In πρὸς φθόνον, 'with envy' or 'jealously', describing a longing of or for the spirit that dwells in us.

study.translationNote: Versions differ sharply at JAM 4:5: some make God the subject who 'yearns jealously over the spirit he made to dwell in us', others make the human spirit the subject that 'lusts to envy'.

background.note: Defined by Greek philosophers as pain at the good fortune of others.

study.caution: The meaning of JAM 4:5 is one of the hardest problems in James; since φθόνος usually denotes a bad human envy, some find it odd as a description of God, while others read it of God's jealous love.

study.summary: φθορά is decay or corruption: the perishability of the created world and the mortal body, ruin as an outcome, and moral depravity.

senses.label: Decay, perishability
senses.definition: The condition of being subject to decay and dissolution, in creation and in the present body; by metonymy 'the perishable' itself.

senses.label: Ruin, destruction
senses.definition: Destruction as the end result of a course of life, the opposite of eternal life, or the slaughter of beasts.

senses.label: Moral corruption
senses.definition: Depravity arising from sinful desire, to which false teachers are enslaved.

background.note: Used of destruction and of death on a large scale, as in a plague.

study.exegesisTip: In 1 Corinthians 15 φθορά stands opposite ἀφθαρσία ('imperishability'): the body is sown in decay and raised imperishable.

study.summary: χάριν, the accusative of χάρις used as a preposition with the genitive, means 'for the sake of' or 'on account of', giving a reason or a purpose.

senses.label: On account of, for this reason
senses.definition: Gives the cause or ground of something, often in the phrase τούτου χάριν, 'for this reason'.

senses.label: For the sake of, to gain
senses.definition: Gives the aim or purpose of an action, such as gain or advantage, or the reason Titus was left in Crete.

senses.label: Because of transgressions
senses.definition: The law was added 'for the sake of transgressions', either to expose and define sin or to restrain it.

background.note: In the papyri the word often comes before its noun, while in the NT it usually follows it.

study.exegesisTip: In the NT χάριν normally follows its noun (τούτου χάριν); 1JO 3:12 (χάριν τίνος, 'for what reason?') is the exception.
study.caution: Whether GAL 3:19 means the law was given to reveal and increase transgressions, or to curb them, is debated.

study.summary: χρηματίζω in the NT mostly describes God giving a warning or instruction, and also means to bear a name or be called.

senses.label: Be divinely warned, instructed
senses.definition: In the passive, to receive a revelation, warning or directive from God, by dream, angel or the Spirit.

senses.label: Warn, speak from God
senses.definition: In the active, to give a divine warning; used of God who warned Israel on earth.

senses.label: Bear a name, be called
senses.definition: To be publicly known or styled by a name, as the disciples were first called Christians, or a woman called an adulteress.

background.note: Originally to transact business or negotiate; later of official answers and oracles.
Used of transacting business and distributing supplies.

study.summary: ἀγέλη is a herd; in the NT it is always the herd of pigs into which Jesus sent the demons.

senses.label: Herd of pigs
senses.definition: A large herd of swine feeding near the lake, which the demons entered and which rushed down the slope into the water.

background.note: Used of herds of cattle and horses, and also of swine.

study.summary: ἁγνός means pure: morally clean, chaste or innocent, of persons and of things such as wisdom or conduct.

senses.label: Chaste, morally pure
senses.definition: Free from moral and especially sexual defilement, as a pure virgin, a godly wife, or a leader who keeps himself pure.

senses.label: Innocent, blameless
senses.definition: Guiltless in a particular matter; the Corinthians proved themselves innocent.

senses.label: Pure in quality
senses.definition: Undefiled and holy, of things worthy of thought, of heavenly wisdom, and of Christ himself as the standard of purity.

background.note: Often used of what is hallowed and dedicated to the gods.
An inscription calls Athena 'the pure Virgin', a phrase close to 2CO 11:2.

study.summary: ἀδόκιμος means 'failing the test': rejected after testing, disqualified, worthless.

senses.label: Disqualified, failing the test
senses.definition: Of persons shown by testing to be unapproved or unfit, whether in faith, ministry or good works.

senses.label: Depraved, unfit mind
senses.definition: A mind that is worthless and unable to judge rightly, to which God handed over those who refused to know him.

senses.label: Worthless land
senses.definition: Of ground that yields only thorns and thistles and is rejected.

background.note: Used of coin that is not legal tender, i.e. counterfeit or rejected after testing.

study.exegesisTip: ROM 1:28 contains a wordplay: since they did not 'approve' (ἐδοκίμασαν) of keeping God in mind, God gave them up to an 'unapproved' (ἀδόκιμον) mind.
study.caution: Whether Paul's fear of becoming ἀδόκιμος at 1CO 9:27 concerns final salvation or disqualification from reward or ministry is debated.

study.summary: ἀεί means 'always', either continually or on every occasion.

senses.label: Continually, perpetually
senses.definition: Of an unbroken or characteristic state or habit, such as always resisting the Spirit or always rejoicing.

senses.label: On every occasion
senses.definition: Whenever the occasion arises, as in being ready at any time to give an answer, or in a regular custom.

study.summary: ἅλας is salt, used in the NT as a picture of the disciples' preserving, seasoning effect and of gracious, wise speech.

senses.label: Salt (and disciples as salt)
senses.definition: Salt that gives flavour but can lose its saltiness and become useless; Jesus calls his disciples 'the salt of the earth'.

senses.label: Seasoned speech
senses.definition: Figuratively, the wisdom and attractiveness that make speech fitting, gracious and apt for each person.

study.summary: ἀναγκαῖος means necessary or indispensable, and once describes 'close' friends.

senses.label: Necessary, required
senses.definition: What must be done or is needed, often in the phrase 'I thought it necessary'.

senses.label: Indispensable, pressing
senses.definition: What cannot be done without, such as the weaker members of the body or urgent needs.

senses.label: Close, intimate
senses.definition: Of persons bound by close ties of friendship.

study.summary: ἀνακλίνω means to lay down, or to make someone recline; in the passive it is to recline at a meal.

senses.label: Lay down
senses.definition: To put someone down to rest; Mary laid the infant Jesus in a manger.

senses.label: Make recline at table
senses.definition: To have people sit down for a meal, as the crowds at the feeding or servants seated by their master.

senses.label: Recline to eat
senses.definition: In the passive, to take one's place at a meal, including the coming banquet in the kingdom with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

study.exegesisTip: At LUK 12:37 the master makes his watchful servants recline and serves them himself, a striking reversal of roles.

study.summary: ἀντίκειμαι means to oppose; as a participle it denotes an opponent or adversary.

senses.label: Oppose, be contrary to
senses.definition: To stand against someone or something, as Jesus' opponents, the flesh and the Spirit against each other, or what is contrary to sound teaching.

senses.label: Opponent, adversary
senses.definition: The participle used as a noun for those who oppose the gospel, for the coming man of lawlessness, or for 'the adversary'.

background.note: Used in a letter of a man 'opposed to us'.

study.caution: Whether 'the adversary' at 1TI 5:14 is a human opponent or Satan is debated.

study.summary: ἀπαρχή is 'firstfruits', the first portion offered to God, used as a picture of the first converts and of a first share that pledges the rest.

senses.label: Firstfruits offering
senses.definition: The first portion of dough or produce dedicated to God, which hallows the whole.

senses.label: First converts, consecrated people
senses.definition: The first believers in a region, or a people set apart to God as the first of his harvest.

senses.label: Pledge of the full harvest
senses.definition: A first instalment that guarantees what follows: Christ's resurrection is the first of the resurrection of believers, and the Spirit is the first share of future redemption.

study.translationNote: At 2TH 2:13 manuscripts differ between ἀπαρχήν ('as firstfruits') and ἀπ' ἀρχῆς ('from the beginning'), so versions differ there.

background.note: Used of the first offering at a sacrifice, such as locks of hair.

study.summary: ἀπεκδέχομαι means to await eagerly, used mostly of believers' expectant longing for Christ's return and the completion of salvation.

senses.label: Eagerly await consummation
senses.definition: To wait with eager expectation for the revelation of the children of God, the redemption of the body, the hope of righteousness, or the Lord himself.

senses.label: Wait patiently
senses.definition: Of God's patience, which waited in the days of Noah while the ark was built.

background.note: A rare, late word for eager or anxious expectation.

study.summary: ἁπλότης means singleness or simplicity of heart: undivided sincerity, and the open-handed generosity that flows from it.

senses.label: Sincerity, single-heartedness
senses.definition: Undivided, unpretending devotion and honesty, toward Christ or in service to masters.

senses.label: Generosity, liberality
senses.definition: Single-minded, ungrudging giving, as in the Macedonians' rich generosity in poverty.

study.translationNote: Versions render the giving passages either as 'generosity/liberality' or as 'simplicity/sincerity', because the word properly means single-heartedness and only by extension generous giving.
study.caution: At 2CO 1:12 many manuscripts read ἁγιότητι ('holiness') instead of ἁπλότητι.

study.summary: ἀποκαθίστημι means to restore to a former state: healing a body, re-establishing order or a kingdom, or returning a person.

senses.label: Restore to health
senses.definition: To heal a withered hand or blind eyes so that they are made sound as before.

senses.label: Restore all things, the kingdom
senses.definition: To re-establish a right order, as Elijah's restoring work or the disciples' hope for Israel's kingdom.

senses.label: Give back, return
senses.definition: To bring a person back to those he belongs with.

background.note: Used of restoring or giving back what is owed.

study.summary: ἀπολογία is a defence, a reasoned reply to an accusation, whether in court or in answer to anyone who questions the faith.

senses.label: Legal defence
senses.definition: A speech or hearing in one's own defence before accusers or a court, including Paul's defence of the gospel in custody.

senses.label: Answer to questioners
senses.definition: A reasoned reply to critics or to anyone who asks for the reason for Christian hope.

senses.label: Eagerness to clear oneself
senses.definition: The desire to vindicate oneself that godly sorrow produced in the Corinthians.

background.note: The standard term for a defence speech, opposed to accusation; Plato's Apology of Socrates is such a speech.

study.summary: ἀποτίθημι, always middle in the NT, means to take off or put aside, mostly of laying aside sins like old clothing.

senses.label: Take off garments
senses.definition: To lay down clothing; the witnesses laid their cloaks at Saul's feet.

senses.label: Put off sins
senses.definition: Figuratively, to strip off a former way of life, vices or every hindrance, as one removes a garment.

study.exegesisTip: The image is clothing: at ROM 13:12 putting off the works of darkness is paired with putting on the armour of light.

study.summary: ἀργός (from 'not' + 'work') means idle: without work, lazy, or useless and ineffective.

senses.label: Idle, without work
senses.definition: Standing unemployed, as the labourers in the marketplace.

senses.label: Lazy
senses.definition: Habitually idle and unwilling to work.

senses.label: Useless, ineffective
senses.definition: Producing nothing: a careless, worthless word, or a life or faith that bears no fruit.

study.caution: At JAM 2:20 manuscripts differ between ἀργή ('useless') and νεκρά ('dead'); ἀργή makes a wordplay with ἔργων ('works').

study.summary: ἀρκέω means to be enough; in the passive it means to be content or satisfied.

senses.label: Be sufficient
senses.definition: To be enough for a need, as bread for a crowd or Christ's grace for Paul.

senses.label: Be content
senses.definition: In the passive, to be satisfied with what one has, such as wages, food and clothing, or present things.

background.note: An impersonal use like JOH 14:8 appears in a letter about having enough lentils.

study.summary: ἀφθαρσία is incorruptibility: the undying state of the resurrection life, and possibly integrity or undying sincerity.

senses.label: Imperishable resurrection body
senses.definition: The incorruptible state into which the body is raised, in contrast to present decay.

senses.label: Immortality as hope, gift
senses.definition: Incorruptible life sought by those who do good and brought to light through the gospel.

senses.label: Integrity, undying sincerity
senses.definition: Incorruptness of character or love, as in 'love in incorruption' or uncorrupt teaching.

background.note: A fourth-century Gnostic gospel contrasts what is born of corruption with what is born of incorruption.

study.caution: EPH 6:24 is ambiguous: 'in incorruption' may describe an undying love, or the immortal life in which grace is enjoyed. At TIT 2:7 the word appears only in some manuscripts.

study.summary: βάθος is depth, whether of soil or sea, a cosmic dimension, or the unfathomable depths of God and of extreme poverty.

senses.label: Physical depth
senses.definition: Depth of soil, or deep water out from shore.

senses.label: Dimension, the depths
senses.definition: Depth as one of the dimensions of reality, used of every power below and of the vastness of Christ's love.

senses.label: Profundity, extremity
senses.definition: Figuratively, the inexhaustible depth of God's riches, wisdom and counsels, or the depth of poverty.

background.note: Used of digging a trench to a proper depth and of setting plants in the soil.

study.summary: βεβαιόω means to confirm or establish, making a word sure or making believers firm.

senses.label: Confirm a message, promise
senses.definition: To show to be valid or reliable, as God's promises, the message of salvation or the testimony about Christ.

senses.label: Establish, strengthen persons
senses.definition: To make believers firm and secure in Christ and in the faith.

background.note: A common legal term for guaranteeing a sale or title.

study.exegesisTip: The legal sense of a guarantee suits 2CO 1:21, where God 'establishes' believers alongside the language of sealing and a pledge.

study.summary: βοηθέω means to come to someone's aid, used in urgent cries for help and of God's and Christ's help.

senses.label: Help! (urgent appeal)
senses.definition: A plea for aid in need, as from the Canaanite woman, the boy's father, the Macedonian or a crowd.

senses.label: Come to the aid of
senses.definition: To give help, as God helped in the day of salvation, Christ helps the tempted, and the earth helped the woman.

background.note: A standard verb in petitions asking officials for help.

study.summary: βόσκω means to feed or tend animals, in the passive to graze, and figuratively to feed Christ's flock.

senses.label: Tend, herd animals
senses.definition: To look after and feed livestock; the herdsmen of the pigs, and the prodigal sent to feed swine.

senses.label: Graze
senses.definition: In the passive, of animals feeding.

senses.label: Feed Christ's flock
senses.definition: Figuratively, Peter's pastoral charge to nourish Christ's people.

background.note: Used of pasturing sheep.

study.caution: In John 21 Jesus alternates βόσκω ('feed') with ποιμαίνω ('shepherd'); interpreters disagree whether the variation is significant or merely stylistic.

study.summary: βουλεύω (middle) means to deliberate or take counsel, and then to resolve on a course of action after deliberation.

senses.label: Deliberate, weigh up
senses.definition: To consider carefully with oneself whether something can be done, as a king weighs his chances before going to war.

senses.label: Resolve, plan, decide
senses.definition: To reach a decision after deliberation and set oneself to carry it out, whether a hostile plot, a travel plan or a practical decision.
senses.note: In JOH 11:53, JOH 12:10 and ACT 5:33 the resolve is a murderous plot against Jesus, Lazarus and the apostles.

background.note: The oldest dated Greek papyrus, a marriage contract, has the couple living wherever seems best to them as they deliberate together in common counsel.

study.exegesisTip: In 2CO 1:17 Paul defends the integrity of his travel plans: his decisions are not made lightly or 'according to the flesh', saying yes and no at once.

study.summary: βοῦς is an ox or cow, the common working and sacrificial animal of the farm.

senses.label: Ox, head of cattle
senses.definition: A bovine animal used for ploughing, threshing and sacrifice, owned, stalled, bought in yoked pairs or sold in the temple courts.

senses.label: Threshing ox (Deuteronomy 25:4)
senses.definition: The ox treading out grain that the Law forbids muzzling, applied by Paul to the right of gospel workers to be supported.

background.note: In Ptolemaic papyri the word generally means a cow; the accusative plural form βόας used in JOH 2:14 is attested in second-century documents.

study.exegesisTip: Paul's question in 1CO 9:9 ('Is it about oxen that God is concerned?') argues from the lesser to the greater: if the working animal may eat, so may the worker in the gospel.

study.summary: βρέφος is a baby, whether still unborn in the womb or newly born and in arms.

senses.label: Unborn child
senses.definition: A baby still in the womb, used of John leaping in Elizabeth's womb at Mary's greeting.

senses.label: Newborn baby, infant
senses.definition: A newborn or very young child; the infant Jesus in the manger, infants brought to Jesus, Hebrew infants exposed in Egypt; 'from infancy' in 2TI 3:15.

senses.label: Newborn babes (figurative)
senses.definition: Believers pictured as newborn infants who should crave pure spiritual milk.

background.note: Homer uses the word of an unborn foal carried by a mare, the same sense as in LUK 1:41.
A papyrus from the time of Augustus speaks of a woman exposing her newborn (βρέφος), the practice described in ACT 7:19.

study.exegesisTip: Luke uses the same word for John in the womb (LUK 1:41) and Jesus in the manger (LUK 2:12), treating the unborn and newborn alike as a 'baby'.

study.summary: γογγύζω means to grumble or murmur, voicing discontent in low, complaining talk, often against God or his messenger.

senses.label: Grumble, complain
senses.definition: To express resentful dissatisfaction, often half-aloud among a group, against someone or about something.
senses.note: 1CO 10:10 recalls Israel's murmuring in the wilderness (cf. NUM 14:29).

senses.label: Mutter, whisper
senses.definition: Low, discontented or undecided talk circulating in a crowd about someone.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: John uses the word for the crowd's and even the disciples' grumbling at Jesus' claim to be the bread from heaven, echoing Israel's grumbling about the manna.

background.note: A third-century BC papyrus reports a work gang 'murmuring' that they were being wronged, showing the word's everyday vernacular use.

study.summary: δάκτυλος is a finger, used literally of human fingers and figuratively of God's direct power.

senses.label: Finger (literal)
senses.definition: A human finger, as used to touch, write, probe or dip, including Jesus' fingers in healing and Thomas's finger in the nail marks.

senses.label: Not lift a finger
senses.definition: Idiom for refusing the slightest effort to help others carry burdens.

senses.label: Finger of God
senses.definition: God's own direct power at work, recalling the Egyptian magicians' confession that the plagues were 'the finger of God' in Exodus.
senses.note: Matthew's parallel saying has 'Spirit of God' instead.

background.note: A late Roman ostracon charm adjures 'by the finger of the god', a phrase comparable to LUK 11:20.

study.summary: διακόσιοι is the numeral two hundred.

senses.label: Two hundred
senses.definition: The number 200, used of sums of money, distance, soldiers, passengers, and as part of the apocalyptic period of 1,260 days.
senses.note: Two hundred denarii (MAR 6:37) was roughly two-thirds of a year's wages for a labourer; two hundred cubits (JOH 21:8) is about 90 metres.

study.exegesisTip: The 1,260 days of REV 11:3 and REV 12:6 equal forty-two months or three and a half years, the period of trial in Revelation (compare the forty-two months and 'time, times and half a time' elsewhere in Revelation).

study.summary: διανοίγω means to open fully, literally (ears, eyes, womb) and figuratively of opening the mind or heart and of opening up the meaning of Scripture.

senses.label: Open (physically)
senses.definition: To open completely what was closed, as deaf ears or the womb at a firstborn's birth.

senses.label: Open eyes, mind, heart
senses.definition: God or Christ enabling people to perceive and receive truth, opening eyes to recognize, minds to understand, hearts to respond.

senses.label: Explain, open up Scripture
senses.definition: To lay open the meaning of the Scriptures, especially as they point to the suffering and rising Messiah.

authorNotes.author: Luke–Acts
authorNotes.note: Luke links the opened Scriptures with opened eyes, minds and hearts: understanding Scripture about Christ is itself a work of the risen Lord.

background.note: Plato uses the verb of opening the eyes.

study.summary: διαστέλλομαι means to give express orders or a strict charge, in the NT almost always a command not to tell or a warning.

senses.label: Strictly order, charge
senses.definition: To give someone a firm instruction, usually that they tell no one what Jesus had done or who he was.

senses.label: Warn, caution
senses.definition: To charge someone emphatically to beware of something.

senses.label: Authorize; what was commanded
senses.definition: To give instructions or authorization (ACT 15:24); in the passive, the command given at Sinai (HEB 12:20).

authorNotes.author: Mark
authorNotes.note: Mark repeatedly uses the verb for Jesus' commands to silence, part of his theme of the 'messianic secret' that cannot be contained.

background.note: Common in papyri in the sense 'give instructions to, enjoin'.

study.summary: διασώζω means to bring safely through danger, or (passive) to come safely through it; once it is used of being healed.

senses.label: Bring safely, rescue
senses.definition: To bring someone safely through peril to a destination or keep them alive in danger.

senses.label: Come safely through
senses.definition: Passive: to escape safely, as the shipwrecked reaching land, or Noah's household brought safely through water.

senses.label: Heal, restore
senses.definition: To bring through an illness to full health.

background.note: Letters use the verb of coming safely out of great dangers.

study.caution: In 1PE 3:20 'through water' may mean that the eight were brought safely through the water or saved by means of it; the next verse links it to baptism, and interpreters differ.

study.summary: διηγέομαι means to tell in full, narrate or describe what has happened.

senses.label: Relate, describe, recount
senses.definition: To give a full account of events, especially of what God or Jesus has done.

senses.label: Declare (Isaiah 53:8)
senses.definition: In the quotation of Isaiah, 'who will declare his generation?', meaning who can tell of his descendants or his generation.

background.note: A second-century letter of a prodigal son complains that someone 'related everything' to his mother at an awkward time.

study.caution: The sense of γενεά in ACT 8:33 (descendants, contemporaries, or origin) is debated, so translations of the clause vary.

study.summary: δρέπανον is a sickle, the curved harvesting blade, used in harvest imagery of the final judgment.

senses.label: Sickle (harvest tool)
senses.definition: The farmer's reaping blade put in when the grain is ripe.

senses.label: Sickle of end-time harvest
senses.definition: The sharp sickle held by the one like a Son of Man and by an angel, swung over the earth for the grain harvest and the grape harvest of judgment.

background.note: A third-century BC papyrus mentions a reaping sickle valued at two drachmae.

study.exegesisTip: Both MAR 4:29 and REV 14:15 echo Joel's call to put in the sickle because the harvest is ripe.

study.summary: εἰ δὲ μή(γε) is an idiom meaning 'otherwise' or 'but if not', introducing what happens if the preceding condition is not met.

senses.label: Otherwise, if you do
senses.definition: After a prohibition or negative statement: 'otherwise' or 'if you do', giving the result of ignoring it.

senses.label: But if not
senses.definition: After a positive possibility: 'but if not', giving the alternative outcome.

study.translationNote: Because the phrase means 'otherwise', English versions render it 'if you do' after a negative and 'if not' after a positive; both translate the same expression.

study.summary: εὐθύς as an adjective means straight, and figuratively upright or right; the same form is also used as an adverb meaning 'immediately'.

senses.label: Straight (path, street)
senses.definition: Literally straight, of paths made ready for the Lord in Isaiah's call and of the street in Damascus called Straight.

senses.label: Right, upright (moral)
senses.definition: Morally straight: the right ways of the Lord and a heart that is right before God.

senses.label: Immediately (adverb)
senses.definition: Used adverbially, 'at once, immediately', like εὐθέως.
senses.note: Mark uses this adverb with great frequency in critical editions.

background.note: A fourth-century Christian letter asks for prayers so that 'a straight way' may be made for the writer, comparable to the 'straight way' of 2PE 2:15.

study.summary: εὐλογητός means blessed, worthy of praise, and in the NT is used only of God.

senses.label: Blessed be God
senses.definition: Opening a doxology, 'Blessed be God...', praising him for his saving acts, following the Jewish berakah pattern.

senses.label: Blessed forever (doxology)
senses.definition: 'Who is blessed forever', a short ascription of praise added to the mention of God, often with Amen.

senses.label: The Blessed One
senses.definition: A reverent Jewish way to refer to God without saying his name.

study.translationNote: Versions render this word 'blessed' or 'worthy of praise'. Unlike μακάριος ('happy, fortunate'), it means the one who is to be praised.

background.note: In the LXX it renders Hebrew barukh, chiefly in the formula 'Blessed be the Lord...'.

study.caution: In ROM 9:5 the punctuation is disputed: either Christ is called 'God over all, blessed forever', or a separate doxology to God begins ('God who is over all be blessed forever').

study.summary: εὐνοῦχος is a eunuch, a castrated man, often serving as a court official; Jesus also uses it figuratively of those who forgo marriage.

senses.label: Eunuch (literal)
senses.definition: A man born incapable of marriage or castrated by others.

senses.label: Court official
senses.definition: A eunuch holding high office at a royal court, as the Ethiopian treasurer of Queen Candace.

senses.label: Celibate for the kingdom
senses.definition: Figuratively, those who voluntarily renounce marriage for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.

background.note: Herodotus describes eunuchs serving as chamberlains in Persian courts, the role reflected in ACT 8:27.

study.exegesisTip: The baptism of an Ethiopian eunuch, once excluded from the assembly under Deuteronomy, fits Isaiah's promise of welcome to eunuchs (ISA 56:3–5).

study.summary: ζιζάνιον is darnel, a weed resembling wheat, used in Jesus' parable of the weeds sown among the wheat.

senses.label: Darnel, weeds among wheat
senses.definition: A wheat-like weed sown by an enemy among good grain, indistinguishable until it heads and to be separated only at harvest.

senses.label: Sons of the evil one
senses.definition: In Jesus' explanation, the weeds represent people belonging to the evil one, to be gathered and burned at the end of the age.

study.translationNote: Older versions say 'tares', modern ones 'weeds'; the plant meant is probably darnel (Lolium temulentum), whose likeness to wheat is the point of the parable.

background.note: Later Greek agricultural writings use the word for a weed that grows in wheat, probably darnel.

study.summary: ζώνη is a belt or girdle worn around the waist or chest, which could also serve as a purse.

senses.label: Belt, girdle
senses.definition: A belt worn around the waist, like John the Baptist's leather belt or Paul's belt used in Agabus's prophetic act.

senses.label: Money belt
senses.definition: The belt used to carry coins, which the Twelve were not to stock with money.

senses.label: Golden sash
senses.definition: A golden band around the chest worn by the glorified Son of Man and the seven angels, suggesting priestly and royal dignity.

background.note: Papyri mention a belt holding small change, illustrating the money belt of MAR 6:8.

study.exegesisTip: John's leather belt (MAT 3:4) recalls Elijah's in 2KI 1:8.

study.summary: θαρσέω means to be of good courage; in the NT it appears only as a command, 'Take heart!'

senses.label: Take heart, take courage
senses.definition: An imperative calling the hearer to stop fearing and be confident, grounded in Jesus' word, presence, forgiveness or victory.
senses.note: Usually spoken by Jesus; in MAR 10:49 it is the crowd's encouragement to the blind man.

background.note: A second-century BC papyrus uses the imperative 'take courage' to oneself, as in NT usage.

study.exegesisTip: In each case the command rests on a stated reason: 'it is I' (MAT 14:27), 'your sins are forgiven' (MAT 9:2), 'I have overcome the world' (JOH 16:33).

study.summary: θησαυρίζω means to store up or lay aside, literally of wealth and figuratively of treasure in heaven, wrath, or the world reserved for judgment.

senses.label: Store up wealth
senses.definition: To accumulate or save money and possessions, whether wisely set aside or selfishly hoarded.

senses.label: Lay up (figurative)
senses.definition: To lay up treasure in heaven, or to heap up wrath for oneself against the day of judgment.

senses.label: Reserved, kept
senses.definition: Passive: kept in store for a future purpose, of the heavens and earth reserved for fire.

background.note: Herodotus uses the verb of storing money safely in a treasury.

study.exegesisTip: ROM 2:5 ironically reverses the image: the unrepentant are 'saving up', but what they accumulate is wrath.

study.summary: κἀκεῖ, a contraction of καὶ ἐκεῖ, means 'and there' or 'there also'.

senses.label: And there
senses.definition: Joins a following action to the place just named: 'and there' something happened or is to happen.

senses.label: There also
senses.definition: Indicates that something happened in another place too, as Paul's opponents followed him to Berea.

study.summary: καλύπτω means to cover, literally (with waves, a vessel, mountains) and figuratively to conceal or to cover over sins.

senses.label: Cover (literal)
senses.definition: To cover something physically, as waves swamping a boat, a lamp put under a jar, or hills falling on people.

senses.label: Conceal, veil
senses.definition: To keep hidden; nothing covered will stay hidden, and the gospel is veiled to the perishing.

senses.label: Cover sins
senses.definition: To cover a multitude of sins, through love or by turning a sinner back.
senses.note: Echoes PRO 10:12.

study.caution: Whose sins are covered in JAM 5:20 (the converted sinner's or the helper's) and in 1PE 4:8 (by love overlooking offences, or by God's forgiveness) is debated.

study.summary: καρποφορέω means to bear fruit or produce a crop, literally of soil and figuratively of the fruit of the word in human lives.

senses.label: Produce a crop (soil)
senses.definition: Of the earth producing its crop by itself, stalk, head and full grain.

senses.label: Bear fruit (spiritual)
senses.definition: Of hearers who receive the word, of believers whose lives produce good works for God, and of the gospel itself spreading and producing results.

senses.label: Bear fruit for death
senses.definition: Of sinful passions at work in the body, producing results that lead to death.

background.note: Xenophon uses the verb of land bearing fruit.

study.exegesisTip: ROM 7:4–5 contrasts two harvests: union with the risen Christ bears fruit for God, while life under sin bears fruit for death.

study.summary: κατηχέω means to instruct by word of mouth, or (passive) to be informed or told about something.

senses.label: Instruct, teach
senses.definition: To give oral instruction, especially in the content of the faith or the law.
senses.note: In GAL 6:6 the one taught is to share good things with the one teaching.

senses.label: Be informed (by report)
senses.definition: Passive: to be told or hear reports about someone, here false rumours about Paul.

background.note: A third-century papyrus uses the verb of an advocate's instruction or persuasion in a legal matter.

study.caution: Whether Theophilus in LUK 1:4 had been formally taught as a believer or had merely received reports about Christianity is debated; the word allows both.

study.summary: κήρυγμα is a proclamation, the message announced by God's herald, as distinct from the act of preaching.

senses.label: Proclaimed message
senses.definition: The content proclaimed by God's messengers, such as Jonah's message to Nineveh or the apostolic message entrusted to Paul.

senses.label: Message of the cross
senses.definition: The gospel message that seems foolish to the world, through which God saves those who believe.

study.translationNote: Some versions render it 'preaching' (the act), others 'message' or 'proclamation' (the content); the word focuses on what is proclaimed.

background.note: In classical Greek, a herald's public proclamation.
Used of an official public announcement.

study.exegesisTip: In 1CO 1:21 'the foolishness of the preaching' refers to the content of the message (Christ crucified), not to a foolish style of delivery.

study.summary: κινέω means to move or set in motion, to remove from a place, or to stir up people.

senses.label: Move, set in motion
senses.definition: To move something, wag the head in mockery, or (passive) to move about as living beings.

senses.label: Remove
senses.definition: To move something out of its place, like a church's lampstand or mountains and islands in the final upheaval.

senses.label: Stir up, arouse
senses.definition: To excite unrest, stirring up dissension or a whole city.

background.note: A papyrus account of a Jewish revolt in Alexandria uses the verb of a disturbance being stirred up, as in ACT 24:5.

study.exegesisTip: The head-shaking of MAT 27:39 echoes Psalm 22, where mockers wag their heads at the sufferer.

study.summary: κοινωνέω means to share or take part in something with others, or to give others a share of one's goods.

senses.label: Share in, partake
senses.definition: To have a part in something together with others: flesh and blood, Christ's sufferings, spiritual blessings, or the sins and evil deeds of others.

senses.label: Contribute, give a share
senses.definition: To share one's goods with others in need or with one's teacher, as a partnership in giving and receiving.

background.note: A prefect's proclamation distinguishes those who shelter robbers as partners in their crimes from those who do not share in them, illustrating 1TI 5:22 and 2JO 1:11.

study.summary: κόπτω means to cut (branches) and, in the middle voice, to beat the breast in grief, that is, to mourn or lament.

senses.label: Cut
senses.definition: To cut branches from trees, as the crowds did at Jesus' entry into Jerusalem.

senses.label: Mourn, lament
senses.definition: Middle: to beat one's breast in grief, mourning for the dead or lamenting at coming judgment.

background.note: Papyri use the verb of cutting down wood, its basic sense.

study.exegesisTip: MAT 24:30 and REV 1:7 draw on ZEC 12:10–12, where the tribes mourn for the one they pierced.

study.summary: κοράσιον is a colloquial diminutive meaning a girl or young maiden.

senses.label: Girl, little girl
senses.definition: A young girl; Jairus's twelve-year-old daughter raised by Jesus, and Herodias's daughter who danced before Herod.
senses.note: In MAR 5:41 it translates the Aramaic talitha.

background.note: In papyri the word often designates a slave girl; it is late and colloquial, though it has no disparaging sense in the NT.

study.summary: κύκλῳ, the dative of κύκλος ('circle') used as an adverb, means 'round about' or 'around'.

senses.label: Round about, around
senses.definition: In a circle round something or someone, as Jesus looking around or beings standing around God's throne.

senses.label: Surrounding, in the vicinity
senses.definition: Of the surrounding area or villages and fields, or a circuit of places.

background.note: Papyri use the adverbial κύκλῳ of the area surrounding a building.

study.caution: In ROM 15:19 it is unclear whether κύκλῳ means 'in a circuit' (from Jerusalem around to Illyricum) or 'and its surroundings' (Jerusalem and the surrounding region).

study.summary: λιθάζω means to stone, to pelt someone with stones, usually as a form of execution or mob violence.

senses.label: Stone, pelt with stones
senses.definition: To throw stones at someone in order to kill, whether as attempted execution for blasphemy or as mob attack.

study.exegesisTip: The present tense in JOH 10:32 is conative: 'for which of these works are you trying to stone me?'

study.summary: Adverb 'always, at all times': marks habitual or unceasing action (above all Paul's constant prayer, thanksgiving and joy) or an abiding state, often set against a presence that is only temporary.

senses.label: Continually, on every occasion
senses.definition: Of action repeated or kept up without lapse, especially prayer, thanksgiving and rejoicing; 'at all times'.
senses.note: Paul likes to stack it with forms of πᾶς: ἐν παντὶ πάντοτε πᾶσαν (2CO 9:8).

senses.label: Abiding state or presence
senses.definition: Of a condition or relationship that lasts permanently, contrasted with what is present only for a time.
senses.note: 'The poor you always have with you, but you do not always have me.'

senses.label: Invariably, without exception
senses.definition: Of consistent, characteristic conduct: what someone does every time, as a settled pattern.

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: About two-thirds of the uses are Paul's, clustered in his thanksgiving and prayer reports, where 'always' expresses the habitual, unbroken character of his intercession for the churches.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: John uses it for the Son's unbroken communion with the Father: he always does what pleases him and is always heard.

background.note: A late word (once in Aristotle); Atticist grammarians condemned it, recommending διαπαντός or ἑκάστοτε instead.
Rare in the Septuagint, occurring only twice, both in Wisdom.
Common in letters: a slave writes to her master that she prays 'always' for his health, the same formula Paul uses of his prayers.
An inscription of A.D. 67 says the gods stand 'always' beside Nero for his protection.

study.exegesisTip: With commands and prayer reports (1TH 5:16; ROM 1:10) πάντοτε describes an unbroken habit or disposition rather than literally uninterrupted activity.

study.summary: Second-person singular reflexive pronoun 'yourself': the addressee's action turns back on himself, in self-discipline and self-watchfulness, love of neighbour 'as yourself', speaking about oneself, and the taunt 'save yourself'.

senses.label: Object of one's own action
senses.definition: The person addressed acts upon himself: show, present, train, throw or save yourself.
senses.note: Several are challenges to Jesus to prove himself by self-serving power: at the temptation (MAT 4:6; LUK 4:9) and at the cross (MAT 27:40; LUK 23:37).

senses.label: Self-watchfulness and self-care
senses.definition: Attention to one's own conduct, safety or spiritual state, often in warnings and exhortations.
senses.note: 'Physician, heal yourself' (LUK 4:23); 'do yourself no harm' (ACT 16:28).

senses.label: 'As yourself': standard of love
senses.definition: In the love command, one's natural regard for oneself becomes the measure of love for the neighbour.
senses.note: From Leviticus 19:18.

senses.label: Speaking or claiming about oneself
senses.definition: What one says, testifies or claims concerning oneself, often in disputes over identity.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: In John the reflexive sharpens questions of identity and the charge that Jesus testifies to himself and makes himself God.

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: In the Pastorals it frames Timothy and Titus's personal discipline: train, keep, watch and present yourself as an example.

background.note: The tragedians use both the full form and the contracted σαυτοῦ; the reflexive was originally written as two words (σέ αὐτόν) in Homer.
The contracted σαυτοῦ is common in the papyri (e.g. 'take care of yourself'), though the NT always has the full σεαυτοῦ.
A first-century court record rebukes a man: 'you deserved to be scourged, having detained on your own authority a respectable man and woman'.

study.exegesisTip: σεαυτοῦ is always singular, so commands such as 1TI 4:16 address one individual; the Koine plural 'yourselves' is ἑαυτῶν.

study.summary: Adverb 'today': the present day, and in Luke and Hebrews the theological 'today' of fulfilment, salvation and decision; with the article, 'this (very) day', 'to this day'.

senses.label: This present day
senses.definition: The current day in its ordinary sense, often contrasted with tomorrow or yesterday.
senses.note: Since the day was reckoned from evening, 'today' can include 'this night' (MAR 14:30).

senses.label: Today of fulfilment and salvation
senses.definition: The decisive moment in which God's promised salvation arrives in Jesus.

senses.label: The 'today' of Psalm 2
senses.definition: The day of the Son's installation in 'You are my Son, today I have begotten you', applied to Christ.

senses.label: Today of opportunity (Psalm 95)
senses.definition: The present period of God's call, in which hearers must respond before the opportunity passes.
senses.note: In HEB 3:13 τὸ σήμερον functions as a noun: 'as long as it is called Today'.

senses.label: This day; to this day
senses.definition: With the article and ἡμέρα (expressed or understood): 'this day', or with ἕως, ἄχρι, μέχρι, 'until today'.

authorNotes.author: Luke–Acts
authorNotes.note: Half the NT uses are Luke's; 'today' marks the arrival of salvation in Jesus, from his birth to the cross.

authorNotes.author: Hebrews
authorNotes.note: Hebrews builds an argument on the 'today' of Psalms 2 and 95: the Son's installation and the still-open 'today' for God's people; Christ is the same 'yesterday and today and for ever'.

study.translationNote: In LUK 23:43 nearly all versions read 'Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise'; a minority place the comma after 'today' ('I tell you today, you will be…'). The earliest manuscripts have no punctuation, so the choice is interpretive.

background.note: σήμερον is the Ionic and Homeric form; Attic prose preferred τήμερον.
Everyday in letters: 'a year today I have been away from you'.
A Jewish prayer for vengeance from Rhenea has the full phrase 'on this day' (ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ), as in ACT 20:26.

study.exegesisTip: In Luke and Hebrews ask whether 'today' is merely calendrical or the theological 'today' of fulfilment and decision (LUK 4:21; HEB 3:13).
study.caution: The 'today' of Psalm 2 is applied to Christ's resurrection in ACT 13:33; whether HEB 1:5 and HEB 5:5 mean the resurrection-exaltation, the incarnation or an eternal 'today' is debated, as is the punctuation of LUK 23:43.

study.summary: Adverb 'separately, apart'; chiefly a preposition with the genitive: 'without' (absence), 'apart from' (independence of a source or means), and occasionally 'besides, not counting'.

senses.label: Separately, by itself
senses.definition: As a true adverb: placed apart on its own.
senses.note: The face-cloth was 'folded up in a place by itself'.

senses.label: Without (lacking something)
senses.definition: Marks the absence of a thing, quality or circumstance accompanying an action.
senses.note: 'Tempted in every way, yet without sin' (HEB 4:15).

senses.label: Apart from, independent of
senses.definition: Separation from a person or source on whom something depends; 'apart from me you can do nothing'.

senses.label: Apart from law or works
senses.definition: In the debate over righteousness: not derived from or dependent on the law or human works.
senses.note: James uses the same phrase for faith 'without works', i.e. faith lacking its works (JAM 2:26).

senses.label: Besides, not counting
senses.definition: Excludes something from a reckoning or adds to it: 'besides', 'not including'.
senses.note: 'Five thousand men, besides women and children.'

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: Paul's key phrase 'apart from the law' / 'apart from works' defines a righteousness given by God, not earned by obedience, though attested by the Law and the Prophets.

authorNotes.author: Hebrews
authorNotes.note: Hebrews (13 uses) repeatedly states necessities with 'not without': not without an oath, not without blood, without faith it is impossible to please God.

authorNotes.author: James
authorNotes.note: James insists that faith 'without works' is useless and dead.

study.translationNote: Versions alternate between 'without' and 'apart from'. 'Apart from' (ROM 3:21) better conveys independence of source than mere absence; in MAT 14:21 and 2CO 11:28 the sense 'besides, not counting' is rendered variously ('besides', 'apart from', 'not to mention').

background.note: In Homer an adverb, 'separately, apart' (lambs penned apart by age).
A common business preposition: 'do not sell the young pigs without me'.
Also 'besides, apart from' in accounts: 'apart from the amounts aforesaid'.
Ignatius uses the adverb as in John 20:7: a head cannot be born separately, without members.

study.exegesisTip: Decide whether χωρίς marks absence ('without'), independence ('apart from'), or addition ('besides'); in ROM 3:21 it denotes a righteousness not derived from the law yet witnessed by it.
study.caution: How Paul's righteousness 'apart from works' (ROM 3:28) relates to James's faith 'without works' being dead (JAM 2:26) is a long-standing debate; many see different senses of 'works' and 'faith' rather than contradiction.

study.summary: Adverb of time 'now, just now': the present moment set against past or future; ἕως ἄρτι 'until now', ἀπ' ἄρτι 'from now on'.

senses.label: Just now, at this moment
senses.definition: The immediate present or a moment ago: 'right now', 'just'.
senses.note: 'Timothy has just now come to us' (1TH 3:6).

senses.label: Now, as opposed to before
senses.definition: The present situation contrasted with a former state or earlier statement.

senses.label: Now, as opposed to later
senses.definition: The present, provisional time contrasted with a coming understanding or consummation.
senses.note: 'Now we see in a mirror dimly, but then face to face.'

senses.label: Until now (ἕως ἄρτι)
senses.definition: Up to the present moment, implying continuation to now.
senses.note: Also ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας, 'to this very hour' (1CO 4:11).

senses.label: From now on (ἀπ' ἄρτι)
senses.definition: Beginning at the present moment and continuing onward.
senses.note: Some editions print ἀπάρτι as one word.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: Nearly half the uses are John's, often contrasting what the disciples cannot grasp 'now' with what they will understand later.

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: Paul sets the 'now' of partial knowledge and present restraint against the coming end, and the 'now' of his gospel against his former life.

background.note: In Attic ἄρτι meant 'just now, a moment ago', often with the perfect ('he has just died'); later it became simply 'now' (= νῦν).
Grammarians noted that Attic writers used it for the recent past, other Greeks for 'now'; it marks the non-literary Koine.
Frequent in magical formulae: 'depart, demon … at once, at once, now' (ἄρτι ἄρτι ἤδη).
ἕως ἄρτι as in Matthew 11:12: 'the petitions have not been got ready until now'.

study.exegesisTip: Notice what ἄρτι is contrasted with: the past (GAL 1:10), the future consummation (1CO 13:12), or simply the immediate moment (MAT 3:15).
study.caution: In MAT 26:64 'from now on you will see the Son of Man seated…' raises debate over how the vindication begins at once; some read ἀπαρτί as 'assuredly' instead.

study.summary: Adverb of καλός, 'well, rightly, fittingly': doing something well or commendably, speaking correctly, exclaiming 'well said!', doing good to others, and the courteous formula 'you will do well to' (= please).

senses.label: Well, finely, competently
senses.definition: Of action done in a good, fitting or effective way; καλῶς ἔχειν 'be well, recover'.
senses.note: Used of leaders who 'manage well' their households and churches.

senses.label: Rightly, correctly (speech)
senses.definition: Of what is said truly or aptly; also as an exclamation of approval, 'Well said! Right!'.

senses.label: Do good, act rightly
senses.definition: καλῶς ποιεῖν: to treat others well, benefit them, or to act rightly in a decision.

senses.label: Courtesy formula: please, kindly
senses.definition: καλῶς ποιεῖν with a participle commends an action or politely requests it: 'you did well to come', 'please send them on'.
senses.note: A standard formula of Greek letters.

senses.label: Ironic: 'fine', 'nicely'
senses.definition: Said with irony of conduct that is in fact wrong or inadequate.
senses.note: 'You nicely set aside the command of God' (MAR 7:9).

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: In the Pastorals καλῶς describes qualified leadership: overseers, deacons and elders who manage and serve 'well'.

study.translationNote: In JAM 2:19 versions range from 'you do well' (ESV, KJV) to 'Good!' (NIV) or 'Good for you!' (MSB), reflecting how strongly they hear irony. In 3JO 1:6 'you will do well' is the polite letter formula, close to 'please'.

background.note: καλῶς ποιήσεις with a participle is the everyday letter formula for 'please': 'please therefore give your zealous co-operation'.
καλῶς ἔχειν, 'be in good condition', appears in phrases like 'in the name of God and of fair play'.
Honorific inscriptions praise officials who 'conducted all things well and fittingly'.

study.exegesisTip: In letters καλῶς ποιήσεις with a participle is a courteous request, so 3JO 1:6 gently asks Gaius to help the missionaries rather than merely praising him.
study.caution: Whether καλῶς is ironic in 2CO 11:4 ('you put up with it well enough') and in JAM 2:19 is debated.

study.summary: Negative connective 'and not, nor', usually paired (μήτε … μήτε 'neither … nor'); the counterpart of οὔτε used where Greek requires μή: prohibitions, infinitives, purpose clauses and participles.

senses.label: Neither … nor
senses.definition: Paired μήτε … μήτε negates two or more items together.
senses.note: 'John came neither eating bread nor drinking wine.'

senses.label: Nor, or (continuing a negative)
senses.definition: Adds further items after a preceding μή or μηδέ, extending the same negation.
senses.note: English usually renders 'or' after the first negative: 'do not swear, either by heaven or by earth'.

senses.label: Not even
senses.definition: Single μήτε intensifying a negative: 'not even'.
senses.note: 'They could not even eat bread.'

study.translationNote: Because English avoids 'neither … nor' after a negative verb, versions often render μήτε as 'or' (MAT 5:34; JAM 5:12); the meaning is unaffected.

background.note: Homer already uses doubled μήτε … μήτε 'neither … nor'.
Classical authors also pair μήτε with τε: 'both not … and'.

study.exegesisTip: μήτε rather than οὔτε appears because the grammar calls for μή (commands, infinitives, purpose clauses, participles), not because the negation is softer.

study.summary: Inferential particle 'then, so, consequently': draws a conclusion from what precedes, often after an 'if' clause; the strengthened ἄρα οὖν 'so then' is characteristic of Paul.

senses.label: Then, therefore (inference)
senses.definition: Introduces a conclusion drawn from what has been said or observed, usually less formal than οὖν.

senses.label: Then (after an 'if' clause)
senses.definition: Marks the consequence in the main clause of a conditional sentence: 'if … then'.
senses.note: 'If righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing' (GAL 2:21).

senses.label: So then (summing up)
senses.definition: Strengthened ἄρα οὖν or ἄρα γε gathers up an argument and states its result or practical application.
senses.note: ἄρα γε also in MAT 7:20, 'so then, by their fruits you will know them'.

senses.label: In that case (unwelcome consequence)
senses.definition: With ἐπεί, states what would follow if a supposition were true, often an absurd or unacceptable result.
senses.note: 'Otherwise you would have to leave the world' (1CO 5:10).

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: About three-quarters of the uses are Paul's; ἄρα οὖν 'so then' is his characteristic way of drawing the conclusion of a stage in his argument, especially in Romans.

background.note: In Homer ἄρα marks immediate transition, 'there and then', as well as consequence.

study.exegesisTip: ἄρα signals the conclusion an author wants drawn, so trace it back to the argument it summarizes (ROM 8:1; GAL 3:7).
study.caution: How far back the 'therefore' of ROM 8:1 reaches (the end of chapter 7 or the whole argument of chapters 5–7) is debated.

study.summary: Particle of affirmation 'yes, indeed, even so': answering questions, assenting to or reinforcing a statement, solemn confirmation, and as a noun 'the Yes' of truthful speech and of God's promises in Christ.

senses.label: Yes (answering a question)
senses.definition: A plain affirmative reply to a question.

senses.label: Yes indeed (reinforcing)
senses.definition: Confirms and intensifies a preceding statement, often before 'I tell you'.

senses.label: Assent: 'Yes, Lord', 'even so'
senses.definition: Agreement with or acceptance of what another has said or willed.
senses.note: The Canaanite woman accepts Jesus' word and turns it into a plea (MAT 15:27).

senses.label: Solemn affirmation
senses.definition: A weighty 'Yes', paired with 'Amen', confirming divine promise or prophetic certainty.

senses.label: 'The Yes': truthful word
senses.definition: Used as a noun: one's 'yes' that truly means yes, and God's 'Yes' fulfilled in Christ.

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: Defending his reliability, Paul turns ναί into a noun: Christ is not 'Yes and No' but God's 'Yes' to all his promises, answered by the church's 'Amen'.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: In Revelation ναί is joined with ἀμήν in solemn confirmation and in the closing prayer for Christ's coming.

authorNotes.author: James
authorNotes.note: James echoes Jesus' teaching on oaths: let your yes be yes and your no be no.

study.translationNote: Older versions render 'yea' or 'even so' (MAT 11:26; REV 22:20 'Even so, come'), modern ones 'yes'. MAT 5:37 is rendered either 'let your Yes be Yes' or 'Yes, yes' (an emphatic double).

background.note: In Homer ναί expresses strong affirmation, usually with δή.
Common in oaths: 'yes, by Kore!'
In a report of senate proceedings an official answers simply 'Yes'.

study.exegesisTip: In 2CO 1:17-20 ναί becomes a noun: Paul's dependable 'Yes' reflects God's fulfilled 'Yes' in Christ.
study.caution: Whether the doubled ναὶ ναί of MAT 5:37 means 'let your yes be (simply) yes' or is an emphatic 'yes, yes' sometimes used as a substitute oath is debated; JAM 5:12 supports the former.

study.summary: Interrogative pronoun 'of what kind? what sort?', in Koine often weakened to 'which? what?', used in direct and indirect questions, especially about authority, time, place, way and manner.

senses.label: Of what kind, what sort
senses.definition: Asks about the quality or nature of something.
senses.note: 'With what kind of body do they come?' (1CO 15:35).

senses.label: Which, what (selecting)
senses.definition: Asks which one among several, with little or no sense of quality.
senses.note: Used alone in LUK 24:19: 'What things?'

senses.label: By what authority or power
senses.definition: Challenges the source or kind of authority, power or name behind an action.

senses.label: What hour, what way (indirect)
senses.definition: In indirect questions of time, place or route: 'at what hour', 'by what way'.
senses.note: In LUK 5:19 ποίας implies ὁδοῦ, 'by what way'.

senses.label: By what kind of death
senses.definition: In John, 'signifying by what kind of death' he (or Peter) would die.

authorNotes.author: John
authorNotes.note: John three times uses the formula 'signifying by what death', pointing to the manner (crucifixion, martyrdom) as foretold.

authorNotes.author: Paul
authorNotes.note: Paul keeps the full classical force 'what kind of': 'by what kind of law?', 'with what kind of body?'.

authorNotes.author: Peter
authorNotes.note: 1 Peter retains the qualitative sense: the prophets searched what time or what kind of time the Spirit indicated; 'what credit is it?'.

study.translationNote: In 1PE 1:11 (τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρόν) versions differ: 'what person or time' (ESV), 'what, or what manner of time' (KJV), 'the time and circumstances' (NIV), depending on whether τίνα refers to a person or a time and how much 'kind' ποῖον retains.

background.note: In Homer it often expresses surprise or anger: 'what manner of word have you spoken!'
Papyri show the weakened sense 'which/what' in indirect questions: 'tell me from what estate you delivered it to him'.

study.exegesisTip: Check whether ποῖος keeps its force 'what kind of' (ROM 3:27, 'what sort of law?') or simply means 'which' (MAT 22:36).
study.caution: In 1PE 1:11 scholars debate whether τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρόν means 'what person or what time' or 'what time or what kind of time'.

study.summary: An adverb used two ways: at the head of a clause it means 'but, yet, nevertheless, only', marking a contrast or the decisive point; as a preposition with the genitive it means 'except, besides'.

senses.label: 'But, yet' — strong contrast
senses.definition: Introduces a clause that sets something against what precedes, often turning to the decisive point: 'but', 'yet', 'however'.
senses.note: In Gethsemane it turns from request to submission: 'yet not my will' (Luke 22:42).

senses.label: 'Only, in any case'
senses.definition: Breaks off a discussion to fix on what matters most or what must be held to: 'only', 'in any case', 'nevertheless'.

senses.label: 'Except that' (πλὴν ὅτι)
senses.definition: With ὅτι it introduces a qualification: 'except that', 'save that', 'only that'.

senses.label: 'Except, besides' (preposition)
